overall_assessment: Retain the revised architecture. NUM-CRIT-01 and NUM-CRIT-02 are addressed in the frozen plan, including their interactions with all six previous architecture resolutions. The new pairing epoch changes the external routing identity rather than assigning an unverifiable local generation to an old event. One domain message-acceptance owner now covers every new keyed writer, including echo-first sender reconciliation and trusted author enrichment. Scope, allowed persistence changes, execution steps, DoD and discriminating tests agree with those choices. I found no objective counterevidence in the complete bounded packet that requires reopening an earlier resolution, and no remaining planning blocker. The observations below concretize tests for requirements already present; they do not request a new architectural direction or additional product scope.
recommended_path: Accept the revised plan as critique-converged, retain D-01 through D-10 and all explicit limitations, and continue the remaining assumption-code coherence, review-scope drift and authority preflight gates. Incorporate the nonblocking checks in the existing security/concurrency/browser harness during authorized execution. Obtain the required human approval before implementation. Provider capability investigation, real registration and IN/OUT proof, implementation-side audits and delivery review remain later work.
correctness_position: Acceptable as a planning contract. A new logical pairing invalidates proof before network, retries reuse its epoch, old mappings are retired, and only positively attributed current-instance evidence may enable ingress. Sender-result persistence and echoes reconcile the same resource/message key in PostgreSQL, preserving Message.id, createdAt and trusted authorship. The contract explicitly rejects missing or incompatible identities and does not transform a successful send into a second null-key row. These are target properties; the unchanged source snapshots do not implement them yet.
security_position: Acceptable as a planning contract. Immutable resource ownership, verified own-number ingress, tenant-derived Typebot selection/session ownership, administrative POST and anti-CSRF, server-side Meta identity/resource proof, candidate-versus-active credential separation, authenticated encryption/AAD and safe diagnostics fit the declared boundaries. The epoch-specific external name removes reliance on uncorrelated old open/wuid events. Secret-bearing URL logging and mixed-owner Meta raw payloads are now explicitly addressed. Runtime compromise, installation-key compromise and provider readiness remain outside what encryption or this review can prove.
performance_position: Acceptable, subject to the planned measurements. DB-only listing, indexed identity/message lookups, short transactions/CAS and a single per-link lease avoid unbounded provider fan-out or database locks over HTTP. Per-epoch replacement adds legitimate create/read/retirement/cleanup work; it must remain persisted across bounded rounds of at most three 10-second calls rather than become an unlimited loop inside one action. Shared message acceptance replaces competing inserts with an indexed reconciliation. The small local EPS/BCI/FRC/RLS trials do not establish production capacity or continuous health.
elegance_position: Acceptable. An explicit pairing lifecycle and a narrow inbox-owned acceptance operation make the two missing authorities visible: current trusted provider identity and the unique persisted message. Separate candidate and active credential envelopes are similarly domain-specific. The extra epoch and cleanup state is justified by external attribution and is preferable to scattered timing exceptions. Do not substitute a same-instance trust shortcut, an in-memory echo cache, query-before-insert, null-key escape rows or a generic worker/vault/outbox framework for these contracts.
structural_soundness_position: Acceptable. The BU remains the number owner, channels remain transports, conversations remain unique by BU/contact and provider-resource ownership survives channel removal. All new keyed message writers now share one authority. The strict change contract admits the required ConversationsService persistence changes and message-acceptance owner while preserving public DTO/window/timeline behavior. Controller/adapter mapping can remain thin and the domain need not consume provider payloads. Old-epoch ingress must remain fenced through the content-write boundary; this follows the chosen contract and is highlighted below as a concurrency test detail.
operational_fit_position: Acceptable for the declared local-first scope. A pinned dedicated Evolution runtime, its own storage/cache, Node 22/PostgreSQL 16, serial destructive suites, principal-checkout single-writer execution and served-build attestation fit the plan. Safe rejection before identity proof, ambiguous-operation reconciliation, ownership-restricted cleanup and explicit pending states make partial progress operationally honest. Meta eligibility, actual provider identity-response support, HTTPS callback reachability and test assets remain prerequisites for real proof. A missing capability must leave the flow visibly pending and return any material replacement design to review; this verdict does not establish that those prerequisites already work.
test_quality_position: Acceptable at the planning level. REG-SEC-10 starts from an already verified channel and observes invalidation before provider side effects, delayed old evidence, a divergent phone and a valid current-instance proof. REG-SEC-11 exercises authenticated echo-first inside the sender's external port, sender-first, repeated echoes, physical row cardinality, stable IDs, trusted author enrichment and distinct-resource independence. PostgreSQL tenant/trigger/session fixtures and non-secret credential/resource identifiers prevent mocks from hiding tenant or credential mistakes. REG-SEC-12/13 cover gateway logs and mixed-owner signed raw batches. None has been executed here. The nonblocking checks below make final-write fencing, Meta verification-query logging and the existing client's enrichment projection more discriminating without expanding behavior.
code_quality_position: Acceptable direction. Keep the acceptance service narrow and inbox-owned, credential resolution explicit at adapter boundaries, and identity/pairing state owned by channels. Preserve the approved source/runtime separation and avoid redistributing orchestration across controllers or introducing alternative persistence writers. Implementation quality and test effectiveness still require the later adherence, TQA, security, debt and final-review gates.

architecture_resolution_assessment.position: addressed-in-plan; retained and completed by NUM-CRIT-01
architecture_resolution_assessment.assessment: Identity-before-content now applies both initially and after a previously verified pairing is renewed. Epoch-specific routing and current-instance proof defend that lifecycle. LID ambiguity, wrong-number quarantine and no-buffer/no-guaranteed-replay behavior remain fail-closed. Provider proof is still a prerequisite for execution evidence, not a silent assumption of this verdict.

Immutable provider-resource ownership survives channel removal, cross-BU reassignment is rejected, and same-BU reactivation is the only admitted path. New Evolution epochs retire old mappings without transferring their owner. The plan continues to distinguish local CAS from proof of an external Meta event's origin generation; no tenant-crossing exception is added.

Pairing remains an administrative authenticated POST with anti-CSRF, lease and generation. The old GET must return 405 without a provider call. A new epoch changes the pairing lifecycle rather than reintroducing a mutating GET or middleware exception.

NOVO/REAUTORIZAR, occupied-slot reuse, fresh attempt/nonce after code ambiguity, isolated candidate encryption and activation CAS preserve the active credential until the same resource is proved. Pairing trust epoch and official credential version remain distinct concepts. Current session/grant checks at promotion, candidate disposal and stale-attempt rejection remain execution obligations already present in the plan.

architecture_interaction_assessment.assessment: D-06 and D-08 refine existing number identity and message idempotency boundaries. They do not change the one-BU/number or BU/contact conversation model, expand Typebot to an unrelated provider, authorize cross-BU transfer or add proactive conversations. Persisted staged recovery allows extra per-epoch provider work to span bounded rounds. Candidate credential promotion remains separate from Evolution pairing trust, durable identity remains the ownership authority, and the inbox acceptance owner is the message identity authority. The supplied canonical module snapshots are short; the planned endpoint/lifecycle/acceptance consolidation must still occur before new routes, and no module becomes Verified from this report.

carried_observation_assessment.assessment: The real gateway, access/error/application logs and success/error paths are now explicit in the dummy-secret harness. The additional Meta query case above uses the same obligation.

Meta verifies the original signed bytes, then partitions accepted raw fragments by verified resource/BU; unknown or retired fragments persist only safe metadata. This preserves tenant ownership without a raw-event platform.
Actual PostgreSQL trigger/session fixtures and non-secret credential/resource identity observations make tenant and credential selection discriminating at the real external port.

failure_modes_and_execution_assertions: RENEW failure or timeout after trust reset must remain pending; old callbacks and expired leases cannot restore the old proof. Cleanup ambiguity must not cause adoption/deletion of an unowned instance or duplicate creation.

Current provider identity responses must be matched to the exact reserved instance; state=open, an operator-supplied name or a response for another resource is not sufficient. A divergent phone remains quarantined.

Duplicate IN or OUT/echo conflicts must reconcile by the database key and validate BU/conversation/contact/direction. A conflict must not fall back to an unkeyed new row or overwrite a different owner.
Trusted sender enrichment must preserve ID/createdAt and cannot later be erased by an untrusted echo. New-message publication, unread and bot effects belong only to the creation winner.

Candidate activation must reject a revoked/currently unauthorized session, stale attempt, changed generation or credential version, or another number; the previous valid active credential must survive failed reauthorization.

Authenticated mixed-owner Meta batches and pre-identity/retired Evolution events must not persist another owner's content in raw diagnostics. Secret-bearing fields and callback URLs require the same negative logging assertions.

Each recovery round must enforce the existing lease/time/call budget even when resource retirement, cleanup and new identity proof require several persisted stages. Listing still makes zero provider calls.

residual_risks_and_limits.risk: No primary-provider/runtime confirmation was performed. Meta eligibility, Graph permissions/resource/register/subscribe behavior, actual pinned Evolution identity proof/payload shape, HTTPS reachability and usable test devices/numbers remain unknown. A failed prerequisite blocks its real-proof criterion; it is not replaced by a fake or this review.

Identity-pending Evolution input can be rejected without provider replay. The UI/runbook must require confirmed identity before test input and allow manual resend. No buffer, import or guaranteed replay is inferred.
A crash after message commit and before realtime/automation can omit those effects. Winner-only replay handling does not provide an outbox, exactly-once external effects or automatic bot replay.

Distinct simultaneous Typebot messages still have no added ordered-session/exactly-once conversation guarantee. The packet explicitly retains that limit. No objective counterevidence requires reopening it in this delta.

Meta events carry no local generation. Durable ownership prevents cross-BU reassignment; a delayed event after same-BU reactivation is not thereby proved to belong to the latest local lifecycle. This remains distinct from tenant crossover.

Existing resource collisions must abort with redacted diagnostics. Legacy null message keys do not retroactively deduplicate history. Existing channels without scoped credentials remain visibly pending. Encryption-key availability and nonce/AAD correctness still require implementation tests.
A compromised running application or installation key is outside DB-envelope protection. Local bounded trials establish neither production capacity nor continuous provider/token health.

Proactive conversations/ST-CON-04, templates/campaigns, historical import/coexistence/migration, binary media, delivery/read states, legacy takeover and Railway/production promotion remain outside this planning recommendation.
